harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary, writable), node2, and node3 (standbys) on RHEL 10. Built a dedicated cluster CA on node1, issued per-node server certs (CN/SAN matching each host) and a replicator client cert (CN=replicator), distributed via SSH to all nodes into /var/lib/pgsql/tls (outside the data directory so it survives pg_basebackup copies). Enabled ssl on all nodes, and restricted pg_hba.conf on the primary to hostssl-only replication connections requiring a client certificate signed by the cluster CA (auth method 'cert', explicit hostnossl reject for the replication pseudo-db). Verified negative case (no client cert -> rejected) and positive case (valid CA-issued cert -> accepted) before building real standbys via pg_basebackup -R, which auto-populated primary_conninfo with sslmode=verify-full and the replicator cert/key. Confirmed streaming replication and data propagation end-to-end. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured boot_id baselines, restarted node2, node3, then node1 (primary last) one at a time via systemctl reboot, polled until each came back, proved boot_id changed on all three, and confirmed post-restart recovery — postgresql active, correct pg_is_in_recovery() state, TLS+cert replication reconnected (pg_stat_replication/pg_stat_ssl showing ssl=t, client_dn=/CN=replicator for both standbys), primary writable again, and a post-restart write replicated to both standbys.
actions_performed: Inspected all three RHEL 10 nodes and installed postgresql-server/contrib + openssl
Set up passwordless inter-node SSH using cluster keypair and /etc/hosts from CLUSTER_HOSTS
Initialized PostgreSQL data directories on all nodes
Created a self-signed CA on node1 (CN=postgresql-cluster-ca, 10y validity)
Issued per-node server certs (node1/node2/node3, SAN=DNS+IP) and a replicator client cert (CN=replicator), all CA-signed
Distributed ca.crt/server.crt/server.key/replicator.crt/replicator.key to /var/lib/pgsql/tls on each node with correct ownership/permissions
Configured postgresql.conf on node1 for ssl on and wal_level=replica/max_wal_senders/max_replication_slots/hot_standby
Configured pg_hba.conf on node1 to require hostssl + cert auth for replication from node2/node3 IPs only, with explicit hostnossl reject fallback
Opened firewalld postgresql service on all three nodes (port 5432 was blocked)
Created replicator role (LOGIN REPLICATION) on node1
Verified negative case: replication connection without a client cert is rejected ('connection requires a valid client certificate')
Verified positive case: pg_basebackup over TLS with the replicator cert succeeds
Wiped node2/node3 data dirs and rebuilt them via pg_basebackup -R --wal-method=stream against node1 over TLS with cert auth, producing standby.signal and primary_conninfo with sslmode=verify-full
Configured ssl settings in node2/node3 postgresql.conf pointing at their own per-node certs, enabled and started postgresql on both
Verified streaming replication (pg_stat_replication) and TLS client cert identity (pg_stat_ssl client_dn=/CN=replicator) on node1
Wrote test data on node1 primary and confirmed propagation to node2 and node3
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node2, then node3, then node1 (primary last) one at a time via systemctl reboot, polling each until exec access returned
Confirmed boot_id changed after each restart (proving real reboot, not just service restart)

Verified post-restart recovery on each node: postgresql active, correct recovery state, replication reconnected over TLS with client cert, and data (including a post-restart write on the primary) present on both standbys

evidence.summary: pg_basebackup -R built both standbys from node1; both started in recovery and node1's pg_stat_replication shows both walreceivers in 'streaming' state

evidence.requirement: Dedicated CA created for the cluster and used to issue certs

postgresql.auto.conf primary_conninfo uses sslmode='verify-full'; pg_stat_ssl on node1 shows ssl=t for both walsender connections

evidence.requirement: Replication connections accepted only with a CA-issued client certificate
evidence.summary: Negative test: pg_basebackup without a client cert fails with 'connection requires a valid client certificate'; positive test: with replicator CA-issued cert it succeeds and client_dn=/CN=replicator is recorded server-side

evidence.requirement: Data actually replicates end-to-end and primary remains writable
evidence.summary: Row inserted on node1 primary appeared identically on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f455a75c...; reboot acknowledged then connection dropped; boot_id changed to 437e2f7a...; postgresql active, not in recovery, accepted new write, both standbys reconnected via TLS+cert

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 368725cb...; reboot acknowledged then dropped; boot_id changed to 0e92b810...; postgresql active, in recovery, repl_test data intact

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id b953e8ce...; reboot acknowledged then dropped; boot_id changed to 47794693...; postgresql active, in recovery, repl_test data intact

evidence.requirement: Post-restart cluster-wide replication health verified after all three restarts
evidence.summary: After primary restart, both standbys re-established TLS+cert replication (ssl=t, client_dn=/CN=replicator) and received a write made post-restart
